keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Hesse row before the 19th-century Electorate and Grand Duchy). The page: it 'consisted of the city of Marburg and the surrounding towns of Gießen, Nidda and Eppstein', 'roughly today's Upper Hesse'; no area. Marburg 8.77E 50.81N 30 km and Gießen 30 km overlap (about 3,300 km2 together), Nidda (9.01E 50.41N) 12 km and Eppstein (8.39E 50.14N) 8 km are small stand-ins, soft. Biedenkopf (a Darmstadt gain in 1604-1648 in the Darmstadt dossier) lies inside the Marburg circle and is not named on this page.

ledger.note: 1567: Hesse-Marburg. 'Philip I, Landgrave of Hesse or Philip the Magnanimous split his large landgraviate into four parts, Hesse-Marburg being one of them' (infobox period 1567-1604). It 'consisted of the city of Marburg and the surrounding towns of Gießen, Nidda and Eppstein'. The page gives no month. Louis IV is its landgrave.

1604: the southern part to Darmstadt. Louis IV 'bequeathed equal shares of his territory to the landgraviates of' Hesse-Kassel (Marburg) and Hesse-Darmstadt (Gießen, Nidda), on condition that 'both territories should remain Lutheran'; 'Hesse-Kassel taking the northern and Hesse-Darmstadt the southern part'. Eppstein is not assigned on the page; entered with the south.

region.text: Gießen, Nidda and Eppstein, the southern part

ledger.note: 1604: the end of Hesse-Marburg (infobox 1567-1604; the text: 'between 1567 and 1604/1650'). The northern part, Marburg, goes to Hesse-Kassel; Maurice of Kassel then 'annexed the whole territory and introduced Calvinism', resigned in 1627, and the two lines 'again fought over the territory' in the Hessian War of 1645-48 (those steps are in the Kassel and Darmstadt dossiers).

certainty.note: The page names four towns and no boundary or area; the circles are stand-ins.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Hesse-Marburg row.

SCOPE. 1567 (Philip I's four-way partition) to 1604 (Louis IV's bequest). The page's infobox lists two periods, 1458-1500 and 1567-1604 (the text: 'existed between 1458 and 1500, and between 1567 and 1604/1650'). The first (Upper Hesse as an appanage of Henry III's line) is in landgraviate-of-hesse as the 1458 'split' event and is not a separate dossier; the 1604/1650 ambiguity is the dispute with Darmstadt (Hessian War 1645-48, settled 1648: Marburg to Kassel, Giessen and Biedenkopf to Darmstadt, per the Darmstadt page cited in those dossiers).

SHAPES. Marburg 8.77E 50.81N 30 km, Gießen (gazetteer place) 30 km, Nidda 9.01E 50.41N 12 km, Eppstein 8.39E 50.14N 8 km; the same Marburg circle is the 1604 gain in landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel and the Gießen circle is the Darmstadt gain. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Marburg', 'Nidda', 'Eppstein', 'Biedenkopf' (Gießen exists).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page gives no month for 1567 or 1604 and no death date for Louis IV. (2) No area, no capital in the text. (3) Eppstein's fate in 1604 is not on the page. (4) The Marburg circle also covers Biedenkopf and some of the Giessen circle, so the 1604 pieces overlap at the join.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
